perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He is a police officer and Jonathan’s childhood best friend; he often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- He recently felt Jonathan was acting differently and became anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important.
- He arranged and attended a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- He told Jonathan he felt something was being hidden. He heard Jonathan admit he had been keeping something: Jonathan is in trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- He heard Jonathan say the situation is complicated and that he did not want to drag Christian into it.
- Christian offered help and support. He heard Jonathan accept that he could use support and resources and needed to figure a way out.
- Christian asked whether the trouble was related to anything illegal. He heard Jonathan say he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian decided to look into the matter discreetly. He heard Jonathan say he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe and told Jonathan that Jonathan was being framed. At that point he had some leads but did not yet know who was responsible, and he planned to gather more evidence.
- Later, Christian found out/believed the real culprit is someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolved to confront that person and bring them to justice.
- He heard Jonathan warn him that this person is dangerous, but also say that Jonathan trusts Christian to do what is right.

He does not have access to hidden events, other characters’ private thoughts, or facts not observed/heard/told to him or discovered through his own investigation.
